# This repo's PR baseline still installs skills 0.1.3: the pin predates the release

## Context

`neo-agent-skills@0.1.4` was published 2026-09-08 (`dist-tags.latest = 0.1.4`, tarball resolves), closing neomjs/neo-agent-skills#44. That ticket's premise was that merged skill substrate never reached the seats consuming it. Publication solved the *supply* side. This ticket is the *demand* side for this repository, and it is the last hop.

`Serves:` no open epic — a one-line adoption step downstream of a completed release, filed so the hop has an owner rather than living in a closed PR thread.

## The Problem

This repository calls the shared baseline through a single, immutable pin:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:73
uses: neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@e409dea5dcbc9f6f97d6eb86ecbef4caa7a269b8
```

`e409dea5dc` is the merge of neomjs/neo-agent-skills#45, which **predates** neomjs/neo-agent-skills#53 and neomjs/neo-agent-skills#55. Measured on that exact revision, it installs the old package at three sites:

| revision | `SKILLS_VERSION` at 3 install sites |
|---|---|
| pinned `e409dea5dc` | **`0.1.3`** |
| merged skills `dev` (`f5fcb7f126`) | **`0.1.4`** |

So every PR opened here runs its baseline guards from `0.1.3` — the version the release exists to retire. Nothing is broken: `0.1.3` is still on the registry, so the jobs pass. The cost is silent staleness, which is precisely what neomjs/neo-agent-skills#44 was filed against, one repository further down.

## The Architectural Reality

**The pin is immutable by design and that is not the defect.** The SHA pin is why merging the release PRs could not break anyone — no consumer follows `dev`. Verified across all four repositories that could call it: `neo` holds the single reference above; `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-institution` and `devindex` hold **zero**, and there is not one mutable `@dev` / `@main` / floating-tag reference anywhere. Adoption is therefore always a deliberate edit, which is the property this ticket exercises rather than removes.

**The job set is unchanged between the two revisions** — `pr-base`, `skills-materialized`, `source-comment-archaeology`, `substrate-size`, `pr-body` in both. This change moves which package version supplies the guards, not which guards run, which is what keeps it a one-line change rather than a CI redesign.

**Ordering is load-bearing and is already satisfied.** neomjs/neo-agent-skills#27 records the live failure mode: a baseline naming a `SKILLS_VERSION` absent from the registry. Its trigger is a caller *reaching* such a baseline, not a merge. Bumping this pin is exactly that reach — so it is safe now, and would not have been before `0.1.4` resolved. This ticket must not be worked if the registry check in AC-1 fails.

## The Fix

Replace the pinned SHA at `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:73` with the current `neomjs/neo-agent-skills` `dev` merge commit (`f5fcb7f126` at filing; re-resolve at implementation time), and confirm by the emitted job output that the baseline jobs install `0.1.4`.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:73` `uses:` pin | this repository owns its own caller pin | names the post-release skills revision | revert to `e409dea5dc`, which still resolves | none — the line is self-describing | `git show <sha>:.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml` reports `SKILLS_VERSION` per revision |
| `SKILLS_VERSION` consumed by the baseline | `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` (skills repo) | `0.1.4`, reached via the pin | `0.1.3` remains published | neomjs/neo-agent-skills#44 | `npm view neo-agent-skills@0.1.4` resolves |

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — precondition, re-checked at implementation time, not assumed from this body.** `npm view neo-agent-skills@0.1.4 version` resolves. If it does not, stop: the change becomes neomjs/neo-agent-skills#27's failure rather than its resolution.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `pr-baseline.yml:73` names the current skills `dev` merge commit, and `git show <that sha>:.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml` reports `SKILLS_VERSION: '0.1.4'` at all three install sites.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the job set is unchanged across the bump: `pr-base`, `skills-materialized`, `source-comment-archaeology`, `substrate-size`, `pr-body` before and after. A changed job set means this is no longer a one-line adoption and needs re-scoping.
- [ ] **AC-4** — the PR's own baseline run is green, and its `source-comment-archaeology` job log shows the `0.1.4` install. Read the job output, not the check name: the two are separate claims.

## Out of Scope

- **Automating this hop.** neomjs/neo-agent-skills#56 owns coupling merged substrate to a published version; this ticket is the manual instance, and doing it does not discharge that.
- **Any other repository's pin.** `neo-agent-brain`, `neo-agent-institution` and `devindex` reference the baseline zero times — neomjs/neo-agent-skills#40 covers the Brain's non-adoption and is a different problem (no caller at all, versus a stale caller).
- **Changing which jobs the baseline runs**, or the local/published guard divergence documented at `pr-baseline.yml:38-44`.

## Avoided Traps

- **Bumping to a branch ref to avoid future bumps.** `@dev` would make every merge in another repository an unreviewed change to this repository's CI, and would have made the `0.1.4` release window a live break instead of a non-event. The immutable pin is the property that made the release safe; the cost of re-pinning is the price of that safety, and neomjs/neo-agent-skills#56 is where that cost gets automated, not removed.
- **Treating publication as adoption.** `0.1.4` being on the registry changes nothing here until this line moves. The two states are independently observable and were conflated once already in the release thread.
- **Reading a green baseline as evidence of currency.** The stale pin passes today, because `0.1.3` still resolves. Green is not a signal that the guards are current.

## Merged — and the post-merge item is NOT yet discharged

Landed as `ad3fbc9c54` at 09:37:20Z. `dev`'s caller now reads:

```yaml
uses: neomjs/neo-agent-skills/.github/workflows/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@f5fcb7f126b41f7ce361684a75983c0c8582b7af
```

**AC-1 through AC-4 were verified on the branch and stand.** The one open box is the post-merge line, and it is genuinely open rather than a formality:

- [ ] *A PR opened against `dev` shows `0.1.4` in its baseline install step.*

**No PR Baseline run has started since the merge**, so nothing has yet exercised the new pin. The nearest run — PR #18454's, at 09:32 — began five minutes *before* it and correctly reports `Uses: …@e409dea5dc` / `SKILLS_VERSION: 0.1.3`. That is the old pin behaving exactly as expected on a pre-merge run, and it is **not** evidence for or against adoption.

Recording this explicitly because a closed ticket reads as a finished one. The mechanism is verified — the merged file names the new revision, and that revision installs `0.1.4` at all three sites — but the **observation** of it running is still owed. The next PR opened or synchronized against `dev` supplies it; whoever sees that run first can tick the box.

This is the same distinction the ticket was filed on: **publication is not adoption, and a merged pin is not an executed one.** It would be poor form to close the loop by assuming the last step of the very chain this ticket exists to make explicit.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-08T10:04:46Z

## The post-merge box still cannot be ticked, and the reason is worth knowing

A PR Baseline run **did** start after the merge — run [`34212688661`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/34212688661) at 09:55:40Z, eighteen minutes after `ad3fbc9c54` landed at 09:37:20Z. It still reports:

```
Uses: …/reusable-pr-baseline.yml@e409dea5dcbc9f6f97d6eb86ecbef4caa7a269b8
  SKILLS_VERSION: 0.1.3
```

**Observed, and I had assumed otherwise:** for `pull_request` events the reusable-workflow `uses:` coordinate is taken from the **head branch**, not from the merged base. That run was on `grace/18232-global-selectors`, a branch cut before the merge, so it carried the old pin even though `dev` already had the new one.

### What that means for adoption

**Every PR branch created before `ad3fbc9c54` keeps running its baseline from `0.1.3` until it is rebased.** Adoption is not repository-wide the moment the pin merges — it reaches each PR only when that PR's branch contains the merge. So the propagation has a tail, and the tail is as long as the oldest open branch.

That is the same distinction this ticket was filed on, one level further in: publication is not adoption, a merged pin is not an executed one, and now — **a merged pin is not an adopted one for work already in flight.**

- [ ] *A PR opened against `dev` shows `0.1.4` in its baseline install step.* — **still open.** Discharged by the first PR whose branch includes `ad3fbc9c54`; any branch cut from `dev` after 09:37:20Z qualifies.

**One observation, not a proven rule.** The alternative reading is that the run was queued against an older ref; I have one sample. The falsifier is cheap and will arrive on its own: a post-merge branch should report `f5fcb7f126` / `0.1.4`. If it does not, the adoption did not work the way the diff implies and this ticket should reopen.

🖖 @neo-opus-grace
